steps.text: Arizona Manor, North Rockbrook, County of Toron

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Ahem...

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Letter for you, Miss Grace.

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Miss Grace is changing.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: She's been sneaking out almost every day while her parents are away. Shouldn't we do something?

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Well, you could start by chopping down the tree outside the window. If you expect me to do something about it through her clothes though, I assure you I've tried everything.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: I haven't seen you try anything.

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Perhaps you should see an eye doctor then, Mr. Counsell.

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Letter for you, Miss Grace.
Leave it on the table.

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Aren't you going to read it?
No need. I can more or less guess what it's about.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: The typical greeting, then asking after my parents, then regretfully declining my request with some excuse or other...
The young Vulpo sits before the dresser, dolefully fidgeting with the receiver in her hands, the indicator light on it flashing red.
She would have been overjoyed if it had flashed yesterday, or the day before.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Maybe I shouldn't be wasting my time writing these letters or reading the responses.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: When will Father and Mother return? I should be ready to greet them.

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Oh, I'm terribly sorry! We were so busy downstairs that I forgot to tell you.

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: His Lordship sent word that he and Her Ladyship have been invited to a bookstore's opening ceremony. A well-compensated appearance, I'm told.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: He would have been better off using his pen name. No doubt it's worth even more than the title of Baron Arizona.

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Well, he used to write some awfully cynical things under that name, so he stopped using it once he became The Right Honourable Henry Arizona.

spans.text: Well, he used to write some awfully cynical things under that name, so he stopped using it once he became

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Better safe than sorry, after all. Who knows how many nobles were involved in what he criticized?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: So he gets to choose his identity, while I'm forced to accept the life he decided for me.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Wait, so how long is this delay?

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: A day.

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: If I didn't know any better, I'd think that grin meant you were planning to sneak out again.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Sorry, I just remembered something urgent!

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Miss Grace!
Temporary accommodation site, Rockbrook outskirts, County of Toron
Near the forests, where civilization meets wilderness, a group of despondent people have been abandoned.
The wet morning mist fades away, and the sun's rays shine into the dark grey forest.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Guys, I'm back!

steps.name: Grumpy Old Man
steps.text: You again? What is it this time? Like this place isn't messy enough already.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Do you remember the health information I asked you for last time?

steps.name: Grumpy Old Man
steps.text: Right, four days ago. Haven't seen your face since.

spans.text: ago. Haven't seen your face since.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Well, I couldn't get back to you because—

steps.name: Grumpy Old Man
steps.text: Because we couldn't hold up our end of the deal? You wanted information on Marianne, and you thought we were hiding something, so you left us hanging to see if we'd loosen our tongues.

steps.name: Gentleman
steps.text: Settle down, friend. She's not your foreman, she's just a little girl. Why would she be playing tricks like that?

steps.name: Grumpy Old Man
steps.text: Don't judge a book by its cover. Who knows what lies beneath the surface?

steps.name: Gentleman
steps.text: You do owe us an explanation though, young Vulpo. Why did you need our health information?

spans.text: owe us an explanation though, young Vulpo. Why did you need our health information?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Like I said, I asked many doctors, and only one didn't reject me out of hand.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: He said if I got your personal information—to learn more about your health—then he could come and help.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Unfortunately, he was out when I brought him the data, and hasn't been back to his office in a few days...

steps.name: Grumpy Old Man
steps.text: What a coincidence!

steps.name: Gentleman
steps.text: Let her finish.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: ...So all I could do was wait, and keep searching for another way.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I did place a transmitter on the door to his clinic though, so I'll get a signal when he opens it! Look, this red light has been blinking since morning.

steps.name: Gentleman
steps.text: What are you doing here then? Shouldn't you be off looking for him?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I wanted to get updated information, since I'm not sure if the reports from four days ago are still recent enough... I don't know much about this, I just thought it would be safer this way.

steps.name: Grumpy Old Man
steps.text: Pull the other one. You only wanted news about Marianne, you never really cared about us. Why should we trust you?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Gentleman
steps.text: You don't need to answer him. He's still under the delusion that the nobles will come and help us.

spans.text: You don't need to answer him. He's still under the delusion that the

steps.name: Grumpy Old Man
steps.text: Phooey! Of course they will! They just don't know about our situation yet.

steps.name: Gentleman
steps.text: Marianne's been missing for quite some time. No matter how much effort you devote to helping us, we can hardly conjure her out of thin air.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I know that. I'm not too worried about her. It's more important to focus on the here and now.

steps.name: Gentleman
steps.text: She's a child, same age as you. Who knows what could happen in the forest?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I knew her before I moved here, and we used to sneak out and play together. She loves plants, and there are enough in there to keep her from going hungry at least.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Her first letter asked me to take care of you, and I'd rather she not nag me when she gets back, so...

steps.name: Gentleman
steps.text: Well, no matter what anyone else says, I'm on your side. I'll help you persuade them too, if it comes to it.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Gentleman
steps.text: Why don't you start your info gathering with me then? I need to go cut some wood once we're done here.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: What for?

steps.name: Gentleman
steps.text: We want to build a bigger house, to fit everyone. Things will get better.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Yes, they will.
Siew Clinic, Rockbrook, County of Toron
An old office lies near the town walls. Grace was last here four days ago, and the dust in the corner has only grown thicker since then.
The windows are covered in grime. They once faced the entire town; now, the melody of industry converges on the west ones only.
A small man sits before the table, muttering in some foreign tongue peppered with a few Victorian words.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: The bill...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: The bill...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: The bloody bill!
Ahem—

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: We're booked for today.
I got what you asked for.
The doctor looks up with a start. The frames of east windows cast long, trapezoidal shadows.
A Vulpo stands at his door, her golden hair glittering in the sun.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Here. I've organized them.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: ...You really did it.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: How did you compile these reports? You're just a child.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I have some medical books at home. I like to flip through them whenever I get grounded.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Just for reference, though. I'm sure there are still plenty of mistakes.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Well done... Well done indeed...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Your turn.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: About that...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I have to visit the Pelham Manor today. Can we talk about this after I get back?
The name Pelham strikes Grace like a bolt of lightning.
An ominous sign.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: My patients do expect me to visit them.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I meant, why do I have wait until after you visit her?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: So... this really is about her?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: You're not her private doctor. She lives in the nomadic city, only visiting here once a month to supervise the factory. Why does everyone do as she says?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It's not that simple.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: You're under her thumb. Just like everyone else.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: She doesn't control me.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: But things are an awful lot easier with her support, aren't they?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Listen, girl.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: To them, I'm a luxury, something fashionable, a lifestyle, value added. That's the foundation on which my life and my family are built. I can't turn my back on it now.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: My rent, my child's tuition, my wife's Oripathy treatment... I can't afford to lose this job.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: This isn't one of those fairy tales where you can defeat the evil and everybody lives happily ever after. The true enemy is formless. It's a byproduct of living. It's life itself.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: And how is helping these poor people at odds with a noble's interests?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'm not Her Ladyship. I can't see the full picture.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: They're just ordinary, harmless people you'd find anywhere.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: And if they're really so unimportant, do you think they'd be treated this way?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: As for other nobles, I doubt any of them would risk getting on the wrong side of the daughter of a newspaper mogul who married into the Pelham family and owns a number of factories.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I'm almost out of free time, Dr. Siew. It was only by happy accident that I could make it today. I wanted to make the most of this spot of luck, along with the hope you gave me.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: If I haven't done enough, then tell me, and I'll keep trying.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: And what exactly have you done?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I asked many people for help.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: So you're placing all your hopes on others.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I suppose you're right...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'm in no position to criticize you. However—

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I envy you. You have both talent and innocence. Your motives are simple. You're young, energetic, passionate. Life hasn't yet pulled the trigger on you.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: But why not do it yourself? What are you so worried about?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: My family may not approve. Or the Pelhams. Or the people of the town...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Hold on, back up. You're just a child. You shouldn't feel bound by such matters. Don't think about it like that.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Listen...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: The night I made my promise to you, I wrote to her and mentioned it. She hinted that luxury is a complicated thing, taking its value from many sources.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: For example, it would be worthless if it were given away to the poor for free.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: She implored me not to lose sight of my 'consumers.'

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: She threatened you.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It wasn't a threat. She didn't need to. It was a reminder. Even if were to become a right bastard, it wouldn't affect her one way or another.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: ...Although I suppose I already am.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I gave you false hope, and now I have to be blunt...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'm sorry, but I only made that promise because I didn't think a child like you would really try to help them.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: So you wanted to refuse from the beginning, but couldn't say it to my face?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'm sorry I got your hopes up.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Do you know the Arizona family? I'm... friends with their daughter. Would you agree to help if she asked you directly?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: If you're friends with a noble, that's all the more reason not to view them so simply.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: The Arizonas have no stake in this, so they have no reason to butt heads with the Pelhams.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: But those people are dying. Shouldn't they care? What about honor?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Nobles are nobles because they're recognized as such. But they don't need the recognition of commoners, just other nobles.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Honor is simply an accessory adorning their power and wealth.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: But what if the Arizonas aren't like other nobles? I'm really close to their daughter, I know they're different!

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Face it, they're all the same.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Did you think Lady Arizona and the baron were really in love?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Their marriage was based on mutual interest, as most of theirs are. One side gained social status, the other gained powerful Originium Arts.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I don't think they're any different from other nobles. If anything, they're still struggling to find their footing, making them all the more conservative.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Are you saying my—

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Are you saying the baron and baroness are...
She could not go on. Logic and syntax break apart, along with something deep inside her heart.
Like the snow castles that Counsell built for her, helplessly waiting for the changing of seasons.
Melted snow fills her eyes.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It's getting late. I have to hurry to Pelham Manor, then go into town to deal with the mess my son caused at school.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'll write if anything comes up.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I apologize. You're young... but you're honorable.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I... I'll find someone else.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'm sorry.
Town Park, Rockbrook, County of Toron

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Unfamiliar Townsfolk
steps.text: Ladies and gentleman, I say again, I found this man cutting down our trees!

steps.name: Unfamiliar Townsfolk
steps.text: He is destroying our property!

steps.name: Unfamiliar Townsfolk
steps.text: Today they cut our trees, tomorrow they'll take our food, then our jobs, then our land!

steps.name: Unfamiliar Townsfolk
steps.text: Defend our property! Defend our jobs! Defend our town!

steps.name: Mob
steps.text: Defend our property! Defend our jobs! Defend our town!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: What are you doing?!

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: No, Miss Grace!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Counsell? What are you doing here?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: That man has ties to the Pelham family. He'll recognize you.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: But I know the man they have tied up! I have to help him!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Let me go!

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Miss Grace... there are people here who know you. That makes you a daughter of the Arizonas, and your every word and deed that of your family's.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Your status does not permit you to interfere.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: What if I say I don't care?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Your servants at home do. They have livelihoods and families. They need steady jobs.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Look at these people. They've never cared about the trees before.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Lady Pelham is most shrewd. She's made the townsfolk despise these people from the bottom of their hearts. Made her will theirs.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Step forward now, and you put Arizona at odds with the entire town.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: This is a complicated matter. If you truly want to intervene, you had best wait for His Lordship to return. They won't keep him tied up for long; it's risky, even for them.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Please, calm down. I must answer to your father.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Your aunt did not know that your parents were going to be late. She's already on her way here, and we will be welcoming her as planned.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: We couldn't very well turn her away... All the servants have their hands full. We had no choice but to simplify the menu and courses.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: And since we have a guest, we require a hostess. I came to bring you back.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: ...Apparently, Miss Grace Arizona has more important matters to attend to.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Please come with me. The manor needs you.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: But...

a.text: His head is bowed, but Grace could feel his piercing gaze, like a sword running her through.
A sorrow far too deep for a girl her age spreads inside her.

steps.text: Arizona Manor, North Rockbrook, County of Toron

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Not this one... This one's no good either...

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: This one...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Why not the previous one?

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: You've been so busy lately that your skin has lost some sheen. I need to find something that can make it shine.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Our guest will be arriving in but a few minutes. We should be at the entrance to greet her.

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Don't rush me, Mr. Counsell!

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Here, this one!
'Miss Grace' does not respond. She leans back in her chair, gazing out the window, while the servants line up to greet the guest.
She casts her gaze towards the town factory as it energetically churns out black smoke in the distance.
It is quiet.
Neither summer nor winter have come as promised.
Her gaze returns to the dresser. The letter that came that morning still lies there.

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: I mended this dress just this afternoon. Look at the sequins I sewed on!

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Are you finally reading the letter? I'll fetch a letter opener.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: No need. I already have it open...

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Mr. Counsell! Stop Miss Grace!

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: *Pant* I-I'm out of breath... *pant* hurry...

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Have the new manservant clean this up.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Out of my way!

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: The banquet is about to start, Miss Grace. As a servant of the Arizonas, I can't let you run around like this.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: What is this about?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I said out of my way!

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: What happened? I can't decide whether to obey unless you tell me.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: A Messenger went into the forest and found some...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: There was a girl was carrying a pile of letters. Nothing written on them, except the sender and recipient. I'm the recipient, and the sender was...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Marianne... it was two weeks ago.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: ...My condolences, Miss Grace.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: It's all my fault.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: I assure you it is not. I witnessed your efforts with my very own eyes.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Did you now? And what precisely have I done?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: From the very beginning, I knew nothing of what they were dealing with.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I could empathize with their suffering, but only on the surface. I just assumed someone would help them, that it would get better.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: For the past few months, all I've done is play the role of the young lady of the house, while writing a few letters in my spare time. None of which amounted to anything.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: But when I finally met them directly these past few days, I realized that what I had empathized with was less than a fraction of their real pain and suffering.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: They need help, Counsell. They shouldn't end up like Marianne.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: It's not your place to do so. You're the daughter of the Arizonas.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: This isn't the place to stand on status. We're all equal before such suffering.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Do the baron and baroness know of this?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: No. I was afraid they would be angry, and make it even harder to do anything.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Perhaps you could tell them once they return.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I heard something about Father and Mother today.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I don't think they're any different from the people I wrote to, seeking help...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Love and kindness are mere illusions when it comes to nobles... even Dr. Siew lied to me.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: But at least he suggested to go among them and check up on their health, to give them some basic advice about medicine.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I even noticed that some of them had gotten better when I visited them today.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: That sort of thing is what's really worth doing... to me, at least.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Why should I wait for others to act? I can't entrust these people's lives and hopes to others. I can't keep fooling myself and putting things off.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Miss Grace, we should wait for your parents to—

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: How long am I supposed to wait?!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: My friend is dead! While she was struggling on the brink of death, I was busy socializing, busy watching my words, busy managing Arizona's relationships with other nobles!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Do I have to stay at home, asking for help in proper, dignified, useless ways, while I watch those who trusted in me get lynched?

spans.text: Do I have to stay at home, asking for help in proper, dignified,
ways, while I watch those who trusted in me get lynched?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Is nobility meant to be a shackle, Counsell?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Maintaining proper etiquette in your social life is all for the sake of the Arizona family's honor and reputation. If it can regain its former glory, it can shine its light on yet more people.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: They don't have the time. Neither do I.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: They were forced to wander because they lost their land. And they'll die slowly while I enjoy the comfort of high society, just as Marianne did...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: What's the point of it all, if the favor of these nobles has to be earned at every turn? If I can bring them back to health, they'll light their own torch, find their own way in the darkness.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Miss Grace...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I'm sorry, Counsell. I'm not angry at you.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I just needed to vent, like how some people turn to drinking or hunting.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I need to do something. I can't live like this without changing.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Let me do something useful, in what few days I have.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Very well, then. You should start by reading these then.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: These are...

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: From the manor library. You remember them, don't you? The baron's translation, which you've flipped through so many times.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: There will always be little details that slip your mind, of course. Bring them along for reference.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Counsell...

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: I've seen this play before. I can't stop you.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: I'll tell them I couldn't catch you. Just don't let it slip that I let you go on purpose.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: ...Thank you.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Hold on, Miss Grace.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: You're not going back on your words, are you?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: I visited Dr. Siew to retrieve the trinket you 'forgot' on his door.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: He told me that if I ever saw the young lady's Vulpo 'friend,' I should tell her that he most definitely did not forget to close the clinic's window, and certainly did not leave various medicines and supplies on the table.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: There will be no hiding your little sojourn. Have you thought about what you'll do when your father returns? I doubt arguing will help the matter.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I'll apologize. I'm not ready to argue with him yet.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Be careful, and keep your identity a secret.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Thank you, Counsell.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Is Miss Grace still in the library?

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Yes. It's like she's a whole different person.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: I only regret that I might have cost you your job.

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: My job? Miss Grace has been spending her days in the library rather than sneaking out. Why would I lose my job?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: A single meaningful journey is worth a thousand frivolous trips. She's not the little girl she once was.

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: Thank goodness for that.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Aren't you concerned?

steps.name: Maid
steps.text: If that's her choice, then her light shouldn't belong to me alone.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Her light, is it?
Counsell gazes to the west and sees the light of the setting sun fall on the floor of the Arizona Manor.
Old memories rise to the surface.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: She's your daughter alright, Henry.
